summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel-use ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint configuration (index.js exports only `extends`/`rules`), but package.json declares a `preinstall` hook that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs is heavily obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, string-array dispatch) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ to disk, chmods it executable, then invokes it against a bundled 727KB payload (math_init.js). If a system `bun` is already installed, math_init.js is executed directly. math_init.js is a `@bun-cjs` bundle whose contents are packed behind a char-code array and a rotating string-array decoder — the standard shape of a packed loader. No native addon, no build step, and no runtime dependency justifies a Bun download or a 727KB opaque bundle for an ESLint config. The alternate-runtime choice causes the payload to execute outside Node, bypassing Node-focused install-time monitoring, and the mismatch between advertised purpose and install-time behavior is consistent with a hijacked/compromised publisher release of a name whose legitimate line is a plain ESLint config.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
